assessment: Near-term revenue is close to zero. The paid layer (dilution data and filing alerts) is crowded: DilutionTracker is given away free by brokers and clones sell for $20-40/mo. QuantDesk's one differentiator, the 'odds' after an event, currently rests on a single signal that loses money out of sample. Showing prices publicly would need a data license starting around $1.75k/mo, and the owner still needs a lawyer and Stripe. The realistic path is Quiver's: free, credible, shareable research first (a pre-registered out-of-sample replication, a tamper-evident track record, Learn pages, and a newsletter list the owner controls), with a $15-30/mo tier only once a few thousand people read it. Until then the most reliable monetary value is career capital: a reproducible quant-research portfolio for internships and quant-dev jobs.
blocked_on_owner: Land or commit the uncommitted research-launch admin-token work currently in the working tree (backend/app/main.py, research_jobs.py, schemas.py, test_research_jobs.py, ResearchRunPanel.tsx/.module.css, api.ts) before this batch starts. Items oos_edge_lab and platform_security_deploy build on it.

Run the long networked studies after merge (the orchestrator can do it, but it needs the owner's go-ahead and a real SEC_USER_AGENT contact in .env): `make reproduce` for the in-sample clustered t-stats (offline, fast), then `python -m app.research.oos` (~30-60 min) and `python -m app.insiders.study` (~1-2 h, roughly 26 quarterly SEC zip downloads plus Yahoo prices). Then copy each result to docs/results/ with a date. The working paper/SSRN preprint is deliberately the next batch, because it should be written from these results, not before them.

Email delivery goes live only with: an SMTP provider account (e.g. Postmark, SES, Resend) plus credentials, a verified sending domain (SPF/DKIM/DMARC), a physical postal address for CAN-SPAM footers (EMAIL_POSTAL_ADDRESS), and a decision to collect subscriber emails while the privacy policy is still a draft.
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: needed for AI filing summaries, signal x AI-flag studies and the research agent. All of these stay config-gated.
DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL: needed for live Discord alerts (already built and gated).

Stripe account, pricing decision and securities-lawyer review of the legal drafts (publisher's exclusion, hypothetical-performance labels, personal-trading policy) are required before any paid tier. A free/Pro entitlement scaffold and a keyed public API were deferred until then: neither earns anything without Stripe, and the API would redistribute Yahoo-derived numbers.

Before any public deployment, a data-licensing decision is needed. Yahoo prices are personal-use only, and the track record shows per-ticker returns derived from them. Either license a feed whose terms permit derived or display data, or hide per-ticker returns publicly and show only aggregates.

Hosting and domain choice, plus production secrets (ADMIN_TOKEN, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL/PUBLIC_BASE_URL), and enabling GitHub Actions on the repo. Also decide whether the repo is public: public code makes the reproducibility claim much stronger.
Optional free external uptime monitor account (e.g. UptimeRobot or Better Stack) pointed at /api/health/details. The endpoint and status page are built here; the external pinger needs an account.
Personal-trading disclosure: whether the owner trades signaled tickers, for the methodology/legal pages.

items.title: Pre-registered out-of-sample Edge Lab (2020-23, fresh companies), firm-clustered t-stats, offline reproducibility

why.legitimacy: The README and the backtest gates both name the out-of-sample rerun as the gate. A pre-registered confirmatory test with clustered errors is the difference between 'we found a pattern' and research a reviewer or quant interviewer takes seriously. Today the 302 events come from only 74 companies, so naive t-stats overstate significance.
why.money: It turns 'odds' on alerts from one in-sample anecdote into a validated (or honestly refuted) number. Either outcome is publishable content for the newsletter, Reddit and SEO.
why.learning: Hands-on practice with pre-registration, cluster-robust standard errors, family-wise error control and deterministic replay: core quant-research hygiene.
why.research: Answers whether the nano-cap offering drift and the 3.02 and material-agreement leads replicate on 2020-23 data with no overlapping companies. The offline replay also yields clustered t-stats for the existing in-sample run with no new downloads.

items.task:
Read AGENTS.md, backend/AGENTS.md, backend/app/research/AGENTS.md (the 'design before results' rule is binding) and docs/AGENTS.md. Build on the current research_jobs.py, which includes the research-launch admin-token work. Do not touch main.py, schemas.py, config.py or any frontend file. Never run the study itself (no network runs, no docker compose run/build). Builders run unit tests only.

1. Write the pre-registration FIRST, as backend/app/research/PREREGISTRATION_OOS.md, dated 2026-10-19 and committed before any OOS result exists. It must fix all of the following:
   - Window 2020-10-01 to 2023-08-31.
   - Size from the SEC public-float frame CY2020Q2 (FLOAT_YEAR 2020).
   - Sample sizes nano 150 / micro 250 / small 250 / large 100, random seed 2020.
   - Fresh companies: exclude every CIK in the in-sample candidate list, i.e. sample_universe(..., float_year=2023, seed=7) including the 2.5x oversample.
   - Same taxonomy, costs, borrow, baseline, winsorizing and benchmarks as the in-sample design.
   - Exactly three CONFIRMATORY hypotheses, with a Bonferroni family of 3 (two-sided alpha 0.05, so t_crit = NormalDist().inv_cdf(1 - 0.05/6) ≈ 2.64):
     - H1: offering_priced, nano, 20d, direction '-'.
     - H2: unregistered_sale (8-K 3.02), micro+nano pooled, 20d, direction '-'.
     - H3: material_agreement, nano, 20d, direction '-'. It was a lead found with a long prior, so it is now pre-registered as a short.
   - Confirmation requires all of: n >= 20; companies >= 15; |firm-clustered t vs zero| >= t_crit; |firm-clustered t vs baseline| >= t_crit; mean and excess pointing the registered way; mean_net > 0.
   - Everything else in the 102-cell grid is EXPLORATORY and reported with the original full-grid Bonferroni.
   - Also fix the outcomes language: replicated / not replicated / underpowered (fewer than 20 events or fewer than 15 companies).

2. Refactor eventstudy.py without changing in-sample behaviour:
   - Add a StudyDesign dataclass (name, window_start, window_end, float_year, seed, sizes, exclude_ciks, results_file).
   - sample_universe() takes float_year and exclude_ciks.
   - run_design(design, event_source=company_events, signal_defs=ALL_SIGNALS) holds the body of run(). run(sizes) becomes a thin wrapper with the current constants.
   - summarize() takes signal_defs (default ALL_SIGNALS), so other studies (the insider_form4 item) can pass their own SignalDef map. Keep this API stable and documented, because the insider study imports it.
   - The output JSON gains config.study (the design name) and config.design (all design fields).

3. Firm-clustered t-stats:
   - Add clustered_t(values, clusters): the CR1 cluster-robust t of the mean, se = sqrt(G/(G-1) * sum_g (sum_{i in g}(x_i - mean))^2) / n, returning 0 when G < 2.
   - Add clustered_welch_t(a, ca, b, cb): the difference of means divided by sqrt(se_a^2 + se_b^2) from clustered SEs. Document that baseline and event samples share companies, so this is an approximation.
   - In every results row add the additive fields t_stat_clustered, t_vs_baseline_clustered and clusters (= companies).
   - Do NOT change how in-sample `significant` is computed. The new fields are reporting-only there; say so in the docstring and in the caveats list.

4. Offline replay and reproducibility:
   - load_prices(..., offline=False) and get_json(..., offline=False). Offline, a cache miss never fetches; it returns None and is counted as coverage['offline_miss'].
   - CLI flag --offline on `python -m app.research.eventstudy` and on oos. If any offline_miss occurs, exit non-zero and list the misses, unless --allow-missing.
   - New snapshot.py with three functions:
     - write_manifest(data_dir, study_json_path): records SHA-256 of every cache file the run read (track reads via a small registry inside get_json and load_prices), the frame file, the code version from env GIT_SHA (or 'unknown'), and the sha256 of the canonical results (json.dumps sort_keys, generated_at removed).
     - verify_manifest(path).
     - compare_results(a, b): canonical diff that ignores generated_at and the timing fields.
   - CLI `python -m app.research.snapshot write|verify|compare`.
   - Manifests go to {DATA_DIR}/snapshots/ and are referenced from the results JSON as inputs_manifest. Cached Yahoo data must never be committed or published (personal-use terms): the manifest holds hashes only.

5. New oos.py:
   - Defines OOS_DESIGN from the pre-registration, plus confirmatory() to evaluate H1-H3 against the rules.
   - CLI `python -m app.research.oos [--offline]` writes {DATA_DIR}/event_study_oos.json (same schema as event_study.json, plus a top-level `confirmatory` list: hypothesis, cells used, n, companies, t_clustered, t_vs_baseline_clustered, mean_net, verdict, plus `preregistration: 'backend/app/research/PREREGISTRATION_OOS.md'`).
   - It never overwrites event_study.json, the live evidence.

6. research_jobs.py: add the kinds 'event_study_oos' -> 'app.research.oos' and 'insider_study' -> 'app.insiders.study' (the insiders module lands in the insider_form4 item). Only a successful 'event_study' run triggers on_study_success (evidence reload). Keep the existing token/enable policy untouched.

7. Tooling:
   - Makefile targets: test (bash scripts/pytest.sh), test-file F=..., reproduce (scripts/reproduce.sh main), reproduce-oos (scripts/reproduce.sh oos), snapshot.
   - scripts/reproduce.sh: LF line endings (see .gitattributes); runs `docker compose run --rm api python -m app.research.eventstudy --offline` (or oos), then snapshot compare against the newest docs/results/event_study_*.json for the main study. It prints IDENTICAL or DIFF with the differing keys.
   - Add snapshots/ to .gitignore.

8. Update backend/app/research/AGENTS.md: the StudyDesign API, clustered fields, offline mode, snapshot CLI, OOS design pointer. Report needed README/docs/.env.example/agent-graph changes (the Makefile joins the tooling module) to the docs item instead of editing shared docs.

Tests (synthetic PriceSeries only, no network):
- clustered_t equals the plain t when every observation is its own cluster (within the CR1 factor), and is smaller when events are duplicated within a firm.
- sample_universe excludes the given CIKs and is deterministic for a seed.
- run_design with a stub event_source and stub prices reproduces the old run() output fields.
- Offline mode never calls httpx (monkeypatch it to raise) and counts misses.
- The manifest round-trips, and verify detects a modified cache file.
- compare_results ignores generated_at.
- confirmatory() verdicts for the replicated / not replicated / underpowered cases.
- research_jobs exposes the new kinds, and only event_study fires on_study_success.

Verify:
- `bash scripts/pytest.sh tests/test_eventstudy.py tests/test_oos.py tests/test_snapshot.py tests/test_research_jobs.py`
- then the full suite: `bash scripts/pytest.sh`
- `bash -n scripts/reproduce.sh`
- `make -n reproduce`, if make exists on the host.
acceptance: PREREGISTRATION_OOS.md exists, is dated, and fixes window, frame year, seed, exclusion rule, H1-H3, the family-of-3 critical value and the verdict rules. oos.py implements exactly that design (a test asserts OOS_DESIGN matches the documented constants).

The in-sample run() output is unchanged except for the additive fields (config.study, config.design, t_stat_clustered, t_vs_baseline_clustered, clusters, inputs_manifest). The `significant` logic is untouched.
clustered_t and clustered_welch_t are unit-tested, including the duplicated-firm case that shows the clustered t is smaller.
--offline never touches the network (test monkeypatches httpx to raise) and fails loudly on cache misses unless --allow-missing.
snapshot write/verify/compare work and are tested. Manifests contain hashes only, and snapshots/ is git-ignored.
`python -m app.research.oos` writes event_study_oos.json with a `confirmatory` block and never overwrites event_study.json.
research_jobs has event_study_oos and insider_study kinds, and only event_study triggers the evidence reload.
Full `bash scripts/pytest.sh` passes. No edits outside owned_paths. No study run was executed by the builder.

items.title: Tamper-evident track record: daily SHA-256 hash chain of journal entries, verifiable exports, seal published in the newsletter

why.legitimacy: A track record anyone can check is the trust moat PRODUCT_RESEARCH.md names ('hash each day's log'). Publishing the chain head in immutable, dated newsletter issues gives an outside witness, so silent edits become detectable.
why.money: Competitors don't publish verifiable alert logs. It is a marketing claim that is actually true, and it is cheap to keep up.
why.learning: Covers hash chains, canonical serialization, append-only design and point-in-time data: the same ideas as audit logs and backtest-integrity tooling.
why.research: It freezes what was predicted and when, so forward results can't be cherry-picked later. This is the forward analogue of pre-registration.

items.task:
Read AGENTS.md, backend/AGENTS.md, backend/app/journal/AGENTS.md and backend/app/newsletter/AGENTS.md. Do not edit models.py, main.py, schemas.py, config.py or frontend files: the platform_security_deploy item wires your functions into routes and the scheduler. Expose a clean, documented API for it.

1. New backend/app/journal/digest.py.
   a. canonical_entries(session, day) returns, for JournalEntry rows whose recorded-at timestamp falls on that UTC day, the RECORD-TIME fields only, sorted by id. Read models.py for exact names. These are the fields fixed when the entry was created: id, accession, ticker, signal, size bucket, filing accepted-at, recorded-at, entry reference price/date, the expected Edge Lab stats stored at record time, and the borrow fee at record time. Mark or return fields that are filled in later are excluded and documented.
   b. day_hash(entries, prev_hash) is sha256 over json.dumps({'day', 'prev', 'entries'}, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=True), with UTC ISO-8601 datetimes normalized and floats rounded to a documented precision.
   c. Chain file {data_dir}/journal_chain.jsonl. One line per sealed day: {day, prev_hash, hash, count, sealed_at, sealed_late}. Genesis prev_hash is 64 zeros. Append-only, written with a flush and fsync; never rewritten.
   d. seal_through(session, data_dir, through_day, now=None) seals every unsealed day from the first journal day up to through_day inclusive. It never seals today or future days. It is idempotent, and sets sealed_late=true when sealed_at is more than 2 days after the day (honest about the Oct 13-19 backfill).
   e. verify_chain(session, data_dir) returns {ok, days, head_hash, head_day, first_mismatch: {day, expected, actual} | None, broken_link}. It recomputes from the DB and the file.
   f. export_day(session, data_dir, day) returns {day, prev_hash, hash, entries}, so a third party can recompute the hash.
   g. chain_head(data_dir) returns {head_hash, head_day, days} or None.
   h. CLI `python -m app.journal.digest seal [--through YYYY-MM-DD] | verify | export DAY`.
   Use UTC throughout, as the journal does.

2. journal/service.py: only add helpers you need, such as a shared query for entries by day. Keep the existing behaviour and tests green.

3. Newsletter. The issue JSON's existing track-record section gains an optional `seal` object {head_hash, head_day, days}, from chain_head(data_dir), or null when no chain exists. Do not change any existing keys, because the frontend reads them.
   - render_markdown and the email-safe HTML print one line in the track-record section: 'Track-record seal through <day>: <first 16 hex chars of the hash>… (<days> days; verify at <PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/track-record)'.
   - The newsletter's banned/advice-word check must still pass.
   - Archived issues are immutable. Never regenerate old issues to add the seal.

4. Update journal/AGENTS.md and newsletter/AGENTS.md: the chain format, what is and isn't covered (record-time fields only; marks are deterministic later computations, not sealed), the late-seal flag, and how to verify by hand with Python's hashlib. Report shared-doc changes (README Track record section, API table) to the docs item.

Tests (in-memory SQLite via conftest, no network, tmp_path data_dir):
- Sealing two days builds a chain with correct prev links.
- Re-sealing is a no-op.
- Editing a sealed entry's record-time field makes verify report first_mismatch on that day.
- Editing a mark field does NOT break the chain.
- Deleting a line breaks the link.
- Today is never sealed.
- export_day's hash recomputes independently via hashlib in the test.
- sealed_late logic.
- The newsletter issue includes the seal when a chain exists, null otherwise, and the Markdown/HTML contain the line.

Verify: `bash scripts/pytest.sh tests/test_journal.py tests/test_journal_digest.py tests/test_newsletter.py`, then `bash scripts/pytest.sh`.
acceptance: journal/digest.py provides seal_through, verify_chain, export_day, chain_head and the CLI, with the documented canonical form (sort_keys, compact separators, UTC ISO datetimes, fixed float rounding).
The chain file is append-only and idempotent. Today and future days are never sealed, and late seals are flagged.
Tampering with a sealed record-time field or removing a chain line is detected. Mark updates are not flagged.
A test recomputes an exported day's hash with plain hashlib/json, proving third-party verifiability.
Newsletter issues carry an optional track_record.seal and print it in Markdown and HTML. Existing issue keys are unchanged, and the advice-word check still passes.
Module AGENTS.md files are updated, and the full pytest suite passes.

items.title: Owned audience: double-opt-in email list, weekly newsletter and daily signal digest delivery, gated by SMTP env

why.legitimacy: A regularly delivered, impersonal publication supports the publisher's-exclusion posture in PRODUCT_RESEARCH.md. Compliant opt-in and one-click unsubscribe (CAN-SPAM, RFC 8058) are what a credible publisher does.
why.money: The email list is the one monetizable asset that doesn't need Stripe yet. Later it carries a paid tier, sponsorships, or Beehiiv/Substack migration. Today issues must be copied and pasted by hand.
why.learning: Covers transactional email, idempotent fan-out, token hashing, and privacy-minimal data design.
why.research: Indirect. The digest pairs each filing with its historical Edge Lab stat, so readers see the research every day.

items.task:
Read AGENTS.md, backend/AGENTS.md (nullable-column migration rule, UTC), backend/app/newsletter/AGENTS.md and backend/app/alerts/AGENTS.md. You own models.py, and you are the only item in this batch that edits it. You do NOT own config.py or main.py. Put settings in your own pydantic BaseSettings class, and expose an APIRouter plus scheduler-callable functions that the platform_security_deploy item will include and wire. The whole feature is OFF unless configured, and nothing is ever sent from tests.

1. delivery/settings.py: DeliverySettings(BaseSettings, env_file='.env', extra='ignore', env_ignore_empty=True) with:
   - SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT=587, SMTP_USERNAME, SMTP_PASSWORD (SecretStr), SMTP_STARTTLS=true
   - EMAIL_FROM, EMAIL_REPLY_TO
   - EMAIL_POSTAL_ADDRESS (CAN-SPAM requires a physical address)
   - EMAIL_DAILY_DIGEST_HOUR_ET=18, EMAIL_MAX_PER_RUN=500
   - property enabled = bool(SMTP_HOST and EMAIL_FROM and EMAIL_POSTAL_ADDRESS)
   Read PUBLIC_BASE_URL via app.config.get_settings() (read-only). Note in AGENTS.md that these fields should move into app.config.Settings later.

2. models.py, new tables only (create_all creates them; no changes to existing columns):
   - Subscriber: id, email (unique, lowercased, stripped), status pending|active|unsubscribed, wants_daily bool default false, created_at, confirmed_at, unsubscribed_at, confirm_token_hash, manage_token_hash, source (nullable short string). All timestamps are timezone-aware UTC.
   - EmailSend: id, subscriber_id, kind 'confirm'|'newsletter'|'daily_digest', ref (issue id or ET date), status sent|failed, error (nullable, truncated), sent_at, with a UniqueConstraint(subscriber_id, kind, ref) for idempotency.
   Store only the SHA-256 of tokens; raw tokens appear only in emailed links. Never store IP addresses or user agents.

3. transport.py: a Transport protocol with send(msg: EmailMessage). SmtpTransport uses smtplib with STARTTLS and a timeout, run via asyncio.to_thread by callers. FakeTransport records messages for tests.

4. service.py:
   - subscribe(session, email, wants_daily, transport) validates the email with a simple regex and length limit, creates or refreshes a pending row, and sends a confirm email. It always returns the same generic response whether or not the address exists (no enumeration). Re-subscribing an active address sends nothing.
   - confirm(session, token) and unsubscribe(session, token): one-click, idempotent.
   - set_daily(session, token, bool).
   - send_newsletter(session, data_dir, issue_id, transport) uses the archived issue HTML from the newsletter archive (read via the newsletter module's public functions or the archive files; don't modify that module). It sends to active subscribers, skipping existing EmailSend rows. Every message gets:
     - a List-Unsubscribe header (https link plus mailto when EMAIL_REPLY_TO is set) and List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click
     - a footer with the postal address, an unsubscribe link and the standard 'research and education only, not financial advice; historical statistics are not predictions' disclaimer
     - a plain-text alternative part
   - send_daily_digest(session, data_dir, day_et, transport): same rules, for wants_daily subscribers.
   - status(session) returns {enabled, active, pending}.

5. digest.py, build_daily_digest(session, data_dir, day_et):
   - Includes the signal filings of that ET day with severity >= 2 and size in nano/micro/small, each with ticker, signal label, EDGAR link, ticker-page link and the matching historical Edge Lab evidence line. Reuse the newsletter's evidence helpers if importable; otherwise implement a local equivalent from event_study.json.
   - Includes the halts count.
   - Renders Markdown and email-safe HTML.
   - Runs the newsletter's banned_words/advice check and refuses to send if it flags anything.
   - Facts and historical statistics only, labelled historical. No prices.

6. routes.py, APIRouter(prefix='/api') with:
   - POST /subscribe {email, daily?}: 202 generic message. When not enabled, 503 {detail: 'Email delivery is not configured on this server'}, and nothing is stored.
   - GET /subscribe/confirm?token=: a small HTML confirmation page.
   - GET /unsubscribe?token= (HTML page with a button) and POST /unsubscribe?token= (RFC 8058 one-click, 200).
   - POST /subscription/daily?token=&on=.
   - GET /delivery/status: public fields only {enabled}.
   Use the app's existing session dependency pattern (see db.py / how main.py gets sessions) without editing main.py. Provide a factory make_router(get_session) if needed.

7. delivery/AGENTS.md: env vars, data kept, the compliance checklist (double opt-in, unsubscribe in every message and honored immediately, postal address, no purchased lists), and the wiring contract for main.py: include_router, call send_newsletter after newsletter_cycle archives a new issue, call send_daily_digest once per ET day after EMAIL_DAILY_DIGEST_HOUR_ET, and skip both when not enabled. Report the .env.example additions and the new `delivery` module for agent-graph.json to the docs item.

Tests (test_delivery.py, in-memory SQLite, FakeTransport, a FastAPI TestClient on a minimal app that includes only your router; monkeypatch DeliverySettings to enabled/disabled):
- Disabled: 503 and no row stored.
- Subscribe, then the confirm email contains a token link; confirm activates; a duplicate subscribe returns the same generic response.
- Unsubscribe via GET page and POST one-click.
- Tokens are stored hashed (the raw token is never in the DB).
- send_newsletter is idempotent (the second run sends 0) and includes List-Unsubscribe headers, the postal address and the plain-text part.
- The daily digest only goes to wants_daily subscribers and contains the evidence line and disclaimer.
- The advice-word check blocks sending.
- Invalid emails get 422.

Verify: `bash scripts/pytest.sh tests/test_delivery.py`, then `bash scripts/pytest.sh` (the new tables must not break other tests).
acceptance: With no SMTP env, POST /api/subscribe returns 503 and nothing is stored or sent. With env set (in tests), the full double-opt-in flow works.
Every outgoing message has List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post headers, a footer with postal address and unsubscribe link, a plain-text part and the disclaimer.
Sends are idempotent per (subscriber, kind, ref). Tokens are stored only as SHA-256. No IPs or user agents are stored.
The daily digest is built from our own DB and Edge Lab data, contains no prices, labels stats historical, and passes the advice-word check.
New tables are added only via models.py with no changes to existing columns, and the full pytest suite passes.
delivery/AGENTS.md documents the env vars, compliance checklist and exact wiring contract for main.py.

items.title: Form 4 insider-purchase event study (SEC insider datasets + XML parser, routine vs opportunistic), pre-registered

why.legitimacy: Insider buying is the best-documented small-cap filing signal (Lakonishok & Lee 2001; Cohen, Malloy & Pomorski 2012: opportunistic trades about 82 bp/month value-weighted, 180 bp equal-weighted; routine trades about 0). A pre-registered replication on recent small-cap data is a credible, citable result whichever way it comes out.
why.money: It adds the first LONG-side signal. That is easier to act on than nano-cap shorts that are hard to borrow, and it is the most searched-for retail filing topic (OpenInsider, Quiver).
why.learning: Covers XML parsing of EDGAR ownership documents, bulk SEC datasets, the CMP routine/opportunistic classification, and reuse of a generic event-study engine.
why.research: A second, independent signal family tested under the same bias controls, which gives the eventual working paper breadth.

items.task:
Read AGENTS.md, backend/app/research/AGENTS.md (design-before-results rule; StudyDesign/run_design/summarize(signal_defs) API added by oos_edge_lab) and backend/app/pipeline/AGENTS.md. Do NOT add insider signals to pipeline/signals.py: that would change the main study's Bonferroni count. This is a separate study. Never run the study or hit the network in tests. Use the SEC User-Agent from settings and keep requests at or below 8/s.

1. PREREGISTRATION.md, written first and dated 2026-10-19.
   Data:
   - SEC 'Insider Transactions Data Sets' (quarterly Form 3/4/5 flattened tables: SUBMISSION, REPORTINGOWNER, NONDERIV_TRANS; https://www.sec.gov/dera/data/form-345). Use 2020Q1 onward for insider history and 2023Q4-2026Q2 for events (the latest complete quarter; quarters filed after it are excluded).
   - Universe: operating companies in the CY2023Q2 public-float frame with a ticker. Random cap per bucket, seed 11: nano 300, micro 400, small 400, large 100 (control). This bounds Yahoo requests.
   Events:
   - Form 4 (not /A) open-market purchases: NONDERIV_TRANS transaction code 'P', acquired 'A', shares > 0, price > 0, by a director or officer (exclude 10%-only owners). Exclude filings flagged AFF10B5ONE when that field is present.
   - Aggregate per issuer per filing date, with a minimum of $10,000 total value.
   - Day 0: the datasets carry FILING_DATE but no acceptance time, so day 0 is conservatively the first close AFTER the filing date (i.e. the next trading day). The filing date itself is never day 0.
   Signals, all direction '+':
   - insider_purchase: all qualifying events.
   - insider_cluster_purchase: the second or later distinct insider buying within 10 calendar days.
   - insider_purchase_opportunistic: CMP classification. An insider with at least one trade (any code P or S) in each of the 3 prior calendar years is classified. Routine if they traded in the same calendar month in each of those 3 years; opportunistic otherwise. Unclassified insiders are excluded from this signal.
   - insider_purchase_routine: control.
   Tests and cost model:
   - Same horizons (5, 20), costs, baseline, winsorizing and benchmarks as the main study. Long only, so no borrow.
   - Significance: firm-clustered t (from eventstudy) with Bonferroni across this study's cells, plus the main study's vs-baseline requirement.
   - Pre-registered expectation: opportunistic > routine.
   Data quality:
   - Cross-check a random 50 events' dataset rows against the raw Form 4 XML (parsed by form4.py), and report the match rate in the output.

2. form4.py, parse_ownership_xml(xml_bytes) using xml.etree.ElementTree only (no new dependency; reject DOCTYPE/ENTITY declarations to avoid entity expansion). It returns issuer {cik, ticker}, reporting owners {cik, name, is_director, is_officer, officer_title, is_ten_percent}, aff10b5One, period, and every nonDerivativeTransaction {security_title, date, code, acquired_disposed, shares, price, shares_after, direct_indirect}.
   - Iterate over ALL transaction blocks.
   - Tolerate empty <value/> elements and footnoteId elements.
   - Treat implausible prices (<= 0, or > 1e6) as None.
   - raw_xml_url(cik, accession, primary_document) strips an 'xslF345X0n/' prefix from the submissions primaryDocument.

3. datasets.py:
   - download_quarter(year, q, data_dir, user_agent) caches the zip under {data_dir}/insider_datasets/.
   - load_quarter(path) streams the TSVs with csv (no pandas) and joins SUBMISSION, REPORTINGOWNER and NONDERIV_TRANS on ACCESSION_NUMBER into typed rows. Verify column names against the SEC readme at runtime and fail clearly if they differ.
   - Offline flag, as in eventstudy.

4. classify.py: routine/opportunistic per CMP, as pre-registered. Pure functions over (insider_cik, trade dates).

5. study.py:
   - Builds a StudyDesign (name 'insider_purchases') and an event_source that yields eventstudy.Event objects from the datasets.
   - Passes its own SignalDef map to summarize(signal_defs=...).
   - Runs run_design.
   - Writes {DATA_DIR}/event_study_insider_purchases.json in the SAME schema as event_study.json (config.study='insider_purchases', plus data_quality {xml_crosscheck_n, match_rate} and preregistration path), so the Lab can render it unchanged.
   - CLI `python -m app.insiders.study [--offline] [--quarters ...]`.

6. AGENTS.md for the module: data source and licensing (SEC data is public; prices remain Yahoo personal-use, so only aggregate stats are published), the pipeline, a pointer to the pre-registration, and how a future live 'insider purchase' alert would reuse form4.py (not built in this item). Report the new `insiders` module and README research-section changes to the docs item.

Fixtures in backend/tests/fixtures/form4/ (small hand-made files modelled on real layouts; no copyrighted content issues since SEC filings are public): two Form 4 XMLs (one with two P transactions and a footnoteId, one with empty values and an A/M grant), and a tiny synthetic quarterly zip with the three TSVs.

Tests:
- XML parse of both fixtures.
- DOCTYPE rejection.
- raw_xml_url prefix stripping.
- Dataset join and P/A/officer/$10k filters.
- AFF10B5ONE exclusion.
- Per-issuer-day aggregation.
- Day 0 is the next trading day after the filing date (synthetic PriceSeries).
- Cluster detection.
- CMP classification edge cases (insufficient history means unclassified).
- study end-to-end with stub prices and offline fixtures, producing schema-compatible JSON.

Verify: `bash scripts/pytest.sh tests/test_insiders.py`, then `bash scripts/pytest.sh`.
acceptance: PREREGISTRATION.md fixes the data source, universe caps and seed, filters, day-0 rule, the four signals, the CMP classification and the significance rule before any result exists.
form4.py parses multi-transaction and sparse fixtures, rejects DOCTYPE/ENTITY, and needs no new dependency.
The datasets loader joins the three tables via the csv module and fails clearly on schema drift. Offline mode never fetches.
study.py reuses eventstudy.run_design/summarize with its own signal_defs and writes event_study_insider_purchases.json in the main study's schema, plus data_quality and preregistration fields.
pipeline/signals.py is untouched (the main study's test count is unchanged).
Full pytest suite passes without network access.

items.title: Platform hardening and wiring: one admin-token policy for all mutating endpoints, rate limits, deep health + status page, study/chain/delivery routes, frontend Dockerfile, prod compose, GitHub Actions CI

why.legitimacy: Today anyone who can reach the API can edit the global watchlist, fire Discord test alerts or trigger ingests. A public deployment with a status page, uptime history and green CI is the minimum bar for being taken seriously.
why.money: Deployment readiness is the prerequisite for any audience (SEO, newsletter signup). The rate limiter and admin policy protect a future paid tier.
why.learning: Covers API security basics, token comparison, sliding-window rate limiting, health-check design, multi-stage Docker builds and CI pipelines: the bread and butter of quant-dev/infra work.
why.research: Serves the OOS and insider studies and the verifiable track-record chain through the API, so results are inspectable rather than hidden in files.

modules: ops (new: backend/app/security.py, backend/app/health.py, frontend/src/app/status/, .github/, docker-compose.prod.yml, frontend/Dockerfile)
items.task:
Read AGENTS.md, backend/AGENTS.md, frontend/AGENTS.md (content rules, server-rendered newsletter pages must stay server components), docs/AGENT_PROCESS.md, and the AGENTS.md files written by oos_edge_lab (research), track_record_integrity (journal) and email_delivery (delivery), which define the APIs you wire. You are the ONLY owner of main.py, schemas.py, config.py and api.ts in this batch. Do not edit models.py, Nav.tsx, globals.css (use CSS modules), the lab or track-record pages, or sitemap.ts/server-api.ts.

1. One admin policy (backend/app/security.py).
   - Generalize the existing ResearchLaunchSettings / research_launch_policy / require_research_launch in main.py into config.py Settings: admin_token (SecretStr, env ADMIN_TOKEN, with RESEARCH_ADMIN_TOKEN still accepted as a fallback alias), research_jobs_enabled (keep the env var), and mutations_enabled (env MUTATIONS_ENABLED, bool | None).
   - Same rule as today: a token always wins (Bearer, hmac.compare_digest). Without a token, mutations are allowed only when the env flag is true, or when PUBLIC_BASE_URL is a local origin (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1, *.localhost).
   - Dependency require_admin(scope) applies to: POST /api/ingest, POST /api/research/jobs/{kind} (keep its current messages and 403/401 semantics), POST /api/alerts/test, PUT and DELETE /api/watchlist/{symbol}.
   - GET /api/status gains admin: {protected, mutations_enabled}.
   - Keep env_ignore_empty behaviour. Existing test_research_jobs tests must still pass unchanged.

2. Rate limiting (security.py).
   - In-memory sliding-window limiter per client key as ASGI middleware. The client IP comes from request.client; X-Forwarded-For is used only when TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=true, taking the right-most untrusted hop.
   - Settings: RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=120 (0 disables), RATE_LIMIT_WRITE_PER_MINUTE=10 for POST/PUT/DELETE and for POST /api/newsletter/preview and /api/subscribe.
   - /api/stream (SSE) and /api/health are exempt.
   - Over the limit: 429 with Retry-After and a JSON detail.
   - Clock injectable for tests. Bounded memory (evict idle keys).

3. Health (backend/app/health.py + routes).
   - GET /api/health stays a cheap liveness check.
   - GET /api/health/details returns {status: ok|degraded|down, checked_at, components: {db, ingest (age of last successful IngestRun), edgar_poller (age of last fast poll), halts_poller, journal (last mark), newsletter (latest issue id/week), alerts (enabled + last delivery result), email (enabled), research_job (active kind)}}.
   - Thresholds: EDGAR stale over 5 min on weekdays 06:00-22:00 ET means degraded; ingest stale over 3x ingest_interval means degraded; a DB failure means down.
   - Each slow cycle appends a compact snapshot to {data_dir}/uptime.jsonl, keeping the last 30 days.
   - GET /api/health/history?days=7 returns the per-component uptime % and incidents (status transitions).
   - Track loop heartbeats in AppState.

4. Wiring.
   a. Studies: GET /api/research/studies lists the available result files from a fixed allowlist {main: event_study.json, oos: event_study_oos.json, insider_purchases: event_study_insider_purchases.json} with generated_at and n_tests. GET /api/research/event-study?study=main|oos|insider_purchases (default main, unchanged response) returns 404 when the file is missing and 422 for unknown names (never build paths from user input).
   b. Research jobs: validate kind against research_jobs.MODULES (so event_study_oos and insider_study work). ResearchJobsOut.latest is already a dict.
   c. Journal chain:
      - The slow loop calls journal.digest.seal_through(yesterday UTC).
      - GET /api/journal/chain returns the head plus the last 30 lines.
      - GET /api/journal/chain/{day} calls export_day (validate YYYY-MM-DD).
      - GET /api/journal/verify calls verify_chain; cache it for 10 minutes because it is expensive.
   d. Delivery:
      - include the delivery router.
      - After newsletter_cycle archives a NEW issue, call send_newsletter when delivery is enabled.
      - Once per ET day after EMAIL_DAILY_DIGEST_HOUR_ET, call send_daily_digest.
      - Run blocking SMTP calls in a thread. Failures are logged and never crash a loop.
   e. Schemas for all new responses in schemas.py.

5. frontend/src/lib/api.ts.
   - Types and methods: studies(), eventStudy(study?), the new optional result fields from oos_edge_lab (t_stat_clustered?, t_vs_baseline_clustered?, clusters?, confirmatory?, config.study?), journalChain(), journalChainDay(day), journalVerify(), healthDetails(), healthHistory(days), subscribe(email, daily), and the new research kinds.
   - Generalize the admin token: move the sessionStorage token handling (key 'quantdesk.researchAdminToken', wrapped in try/catch) into api.ts helpers getAdminToken/setAdminToken, attached as a Bearer header on every mutating call. Add a typed ApiError carrying status. Keep ResearchRunPanel working through the new helpers (update ResearchRunPanel.tsx accordingly, and add the new kinds only where the panel is generic).
   - The watchlist toggle and 'ingest now' must show a clear 'admin token required' message on 401/403 (handled via ApiError in api.ts callers you own; other callers just surface the error text).

6. Frontend pages you own.
   - /status: a client page with overall status, a component table with ages, 7-day uptime bars from healthHistory (inline SVG, accessible labels) and recent incidents. It also has a small 'Admin token (this tab only)' field using setAdminToken, and the track-record chain verification result from journalVerify ('verified through <day>, head <hash prefix>').
   - SubscribeForm.tsx with a CSS module: email plus a 'daily digest' checkbox. It calls api.subscribe, shows the generic success message, and shows 'Email delivery isn't set up on this server yet' on 503. Place it on /newsletter (keep page.tsx a server component and render the form as a client island).
   - IssueView.tsx: render the optional track_record.seal line.
   - Footer.tsx: add Status and Subscribe links.
   Follow the content rules: no buy/sell language, label historical stats.

7. Deployment.
   - next.config.ts: output 'standalone'.
   - frontend/Dockerfile: a multi-stage node:20-alpine image (npm ci, next build, then a runner with .next/standalone, .next/static and public, as a non-root user), with ARGs NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL.
   - frontend/.dockerignore: node_modules, .next, .env*.
   - docker-compose.prod.yml:
     - db: no published port; POSTGRES_PASSWORD from ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?}.
     - api: ADMIN_TOKEN=${ADMIN_TOKEN:?}, restart unless-stopped, a healthcheck via python urllib on /api/health, CORS_ORIGINS and PUBLIC_BASE_URL from env.
     - web: built from frontend/Dockerfile.
     - named volumes. A header comment says to use it with --env-file and never commit the file.

8. CI. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs on push and pull_request, with concurrency cancel.
   - Backend job: ubuntu-latest, Python 3.12 (match backend/Dockerfile), pip cache, `pip install -r backend/requirements-dev.txt`, `pytest -q` in backend/ (SQLite, no network).
   - Frontend job: Node 20, npm cache, `npm ci`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` (CI may build; local agents may not).
   - Docker job: build the api image and the frontend image without pushing.
   - No secrets are required.

9. Report to the docs item: the new env vars (ADMIN_TOKEN, MUTATIONS_ENABLED, RATE_LIMIT_*, TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS, plus the SMTP/EMAIL vars from delivery), new endpoints for the README API table, the new `ops` module paths for agent-graph.json, and the prod deploy steps.

Tests:
- test_security.py:
  - token required when set; RESEARCH_ADMIN_TOKEN alias works
  - local-origin default allows mutations; a public PUBLIC_BASE_URL without a token gives 403
  - wrong token gives 401
  - watchlist PUT/DELETE, ingest and alerts/test are protected
  - limiter returns 429 with Retry-After using an injected clock; SSE is exempt; X-Forwarded-For is ignored unless trusted
- test_health.py: ok/degraded/down from stubbed state; the market-hours rule; uptime.jsonl trimming and history math.
- test_api.py:
  - study allowlist (main unchanged; 404 when missing; 422 unknown, including a path-traversal-looking name)
  - chain endpoints with a tmp chain
  - the delivery router is mounted (503 when disabled)
  - research kinds come from MODULES

Verify:
- `bash scripts/pytest.sh tests/test_api.py tests/test_security.py tests/test_health.py tests/test_research_jobs.py`, then `bash scripts/pytest.sh`
- `cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit`, plus `npx eslint src` if it runs
- `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml config -q` with dummy ADMIN_TOKEN/POSTGRES_PASSWORD env vars (config parse only, no build or up)
- optionally `docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo" -w /repo rhysd/actionlint:latest` to lint the workflow
- Do not run next build or docker compose build/up (the Verify node does).
acceptance: One admin policy protects ingest, research jobs, alerts/test and watchlist mutations. RESEARCH_ADMIN_TOKEN still works, existing research-job tests pass unchanged, and /api/status reports protection state.
The rate limiter returns 429 with Retry-After, exempts SSE and health, ignores X-Forwarded-For unless TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS, and keeps bounded memory. All of this is tested with an injected clock.
/api/health/details and /api/health/history report per-component state with documented thresholds. The /status page renders them, plus chain verification and the tab-only admin token field.
The study endpoint serves main/oos/insider_purchases from a fixed allowlist (404 missing, 422 unknown). The main response is unchanged.
Journal chain sealing runs from the slow loop, and the chain/export/verify endpoints work.
The delivery router is mounted, and newsletter and daily-digest sends are wired, gated and non-crashing.
api.ts mirrors every new type and method. The admin token lives in api.ts helpers (sessionStorage, try/catch), and 401/403 show a clear message.
The subscribe form appears on /newsletter (the page stays a server component), IssueView shows the seal, and the footer links to Status.
frontend/Dockerfile, .dockerignore, docker-compose.prod.yml (passes `config -q` with dummy env) and .github/workflows/ci.yml (pytest, tsc, lint, next build, image builds; no secrets) exist.
Full pytest and `npx tsc --noEmit` pass. No edits to models.py, Nav.tsx, globals.css, lab/track-record pages, server-api.ts or sitemap.ts.

items.title: Learn: SEO-friendly quant lessons and a curriculum built on QuantDesk's own data and code, plus Lab OOS comparison and track-record seal panel

why.legitimacy: Teaching exactly why the backtest says 'not tradable' (frictions, survivorship, multiple testing, clustering) shows intellectual honesty that tout-style competitors lack. The Lab's side-by-side in-sample vs out-of-sample view makes the replication result visible.
why.money: Evergreen, server-rendered lesson pages ('deflated Sharpe ratio calculator', 'event study explained', 'survivorship bias example') are long-tail SEO and shareable on Reddit/X, feeding newsletter signups. This is Quiver's free-content-first growth pattern.
why.learning: This is the owner's own curriculum. Each concept is tied to the file and function in this repo that implements it, with exercises that change code and rerun tests.
why.research: The Lab shows confirmatory OOS verdicts and clustered t-stats next to the in-sample results, and includes the insider study via a selector.

items.task:
Read AGENTS.md and frontend/AGENTS.md (no UI library, strict TS, server-rendered SEO pattern via server-api.ts Result<T>, content rules: no buy/sell/advice language, label hypothetical and historical numbers), backend/app/backtest/AGENTS.md and stats.py (PSR/DSR formulas), and backend/app/research/AGENTS.md. Use only the api.ts methods and types added by platform_security_deploy; do not edit api.ts, Footer.tsx or the status/newsletter files. In globals.css, append only under a new '/* --- Learn --- */' section header; prefer CSS modules. Add one tab {href: '/learn', label: 'Learn'} to TABS in Nav.tsx.

1. Lesson registry, frontend/src/lib/learn/lessons.ts: slug, title, description (for metadata), level, minutes, concepts, and repoRefs [{path, symbol, why}], all paths existing in this repo.
   Optional env NEXT_PUBLIC_REPO_URL turns repoRefs into links (`${REPO_URL}/blob/main/${path}`); without it they render as <code> paths. Report the env var to the docs item.
   Pure, deterministic helpers in frontend/src/lib/learn/:
   - a seeded PRNG (mulberry32)
   - normal and student-t utilities
   - psr(), dsr() and expectedMaxSharpe() mirroring backend/app/backtest/stats.py (cite Bailey & López de Prado 2012/2014)
   - clusteredT() mirroring eventstudy.clustered_t
   - bonferroniT()
   - winsorize()

2. Pages:
   - /learn: an index server component listing the lessons and the curriculum.
   - /learn/[slug]: generateStaticParams over the registry; unknown slugs call notFound() in a (view)/layout.tsx-style gate as in the ticker pattern, or via dynamicParams=false.
   - Each page sets metadata (title, description, canonical, Open Graph) and Article JSON-LD with '<' escaped.
   - Prose is server-rendered. Live QuantDesk numbers come from new server-api.ts helpers getEventStudy(study) and getBacktestReport() (Result<T>, revalidate 1 h, timeout, React cache()), shown with their generated_at date and 'historical'/'hypothetical' labels. If the API is unavailable, the lesson still renders, with a note.
   - Interactive widgets are client components in frontend/src/components/learn/, using inline SVG with accessible labels and no chart library.
   Lessons:
   (a) event-study: abnormal returns and drift vs reaction. A widget to pick signal/bucket/horizon from the live study and see mean, median, baseline, excess and net, with the day-0 timing rule explained. Refs: eventstudy.measure, day0_index.
   (b) baselines: why 'vs ordinary days' matters (the nano baseline drifts negative). Refs: baseline_events, welch_t.
   (c) multiple-testing: a simulator that generates N pure-noise signals (seeded) and counts 'discoveries' at 1.96 vs the Bonferroni cutoff; QuantDesk's 102 tests and t=3.49 shown live; Harvey, Liu & Zhu (2016). Refs: summarize.
   (d) clustered-errors: a simulator of events concentrated in few firms, naive vs clustered t; then the real nano-offering row's t_stat vs t_stat_clustered (if present), and the OOS confirmatory verdicts (if event_study_oos exists); Petersen (2009). Refs: clustered_t, PREREGISTRATION_OOS.md.
   (e) survivorship-bias: a simulator where losers delist and vanish from the sample, showing the measured vs true mean; the live coverage no_ticker/no_prices numbers. Refs: coverage in eventstudy.run_design, backtest universe.
   (f) sharpe-dsr-backtest-pitfalls: a calculator (SR, observations, skew, kurtosis, number of trials) for PSR and DSR, pre-filled from the backtest report. It must reproduce the report's dsr_A within 0.01 when fed the report's own inputs (if the report exposes them; otherwise document the inputs used). Also the friction waterfall walk-through (gross edge to net loss), in-sample vs out-of-sample, look-ahead and borrow. Refs: backtest/stats.py, engine.py, report.py gates.
   (g) /learn/curriculum: an 8-week self-study path for a student quant developer. Each week has concepts, the repo files to read, an exercise that changes code and runs `bash scripts/pytest.sh <test>` (e.g. 'add a 10-day horizon in a branch and see which tests fail', 'write a test for clustered_t', 'parse a Form 4 fixture'), and canonical readings by author/year: MacKinlay 1997; Loughran & Ritter 1995; Lakonishok & Lee 2001; Cohen, Malloy & Pomorski 2012; Harvey, Liu & Zhu 2016; Bailey & López de Prado 2014; Petersen 2009. No copyrighted excerpts, only citations.
   Each lesson ends with 'What this means for QuantDesk', 'Read the code' and the disclaimer.

3. sitemap.ts: add /learn, every lesson and /learn/curriculum.

4. Lab (frontend/src/app/lab/):
   - A study selector driven by api.studies(): In-sample (main), Out-of-sample 2020-23, Insider purchases. Missing studies are disabled with 'not run yet'.
   - Show t_stat_clustered and clusters columns when present.
   - For oos, render the `confirmatory` block first: H1-H3, verdict badges (replicated / not replicated / underpowered), and a link to the pre-registration file path.
   - An 'In-sample vs OOS' comparison table for the cells present in both.
   - Keep the existing DivergingChart and the run panel; it still works with the new kinds via ResearchRunPanel as updated by platform_security_deploy.

5. Track record (frontend/src/app/track-record/, components/track/): a SealPanel with the chain head (hash prefix, through-day, days, late-sealed count) and the verification status from api.journalVerify(). It includes a short 'verify it yourself' explainer (download a day via the chain/{day} endpoint, recompute sha256 with sort_keys/compact JSON) and a link to /learn.

Verify:
- `cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit` (must pass)
- `npx eslint src/app/learn src/components/learn src/lib/learn src/app/lab src/components/track` if eslint runs
- If Node 22+ is available, check lib/learn psr/dsr with a throwaway script in the scratchpad (not the repo) run via `node --experimental-strip-types`. Compare against values from backend/app/backtest/stats.py computed with a one-off `python -c` in the quantdesk-api-test image (mount backend/ the way scripts/pytest.sh does). Otherwise, document a hand check in the report.
- Do not run next build.
acceptance: A 'Learn' tab is in Nav. /learn, six lesson pages and /learn/curriculum are server-rendered with metadata, canonical and JSON-LD, and are listed in sitemap.xml.
Each lesson ties to real repo files/functions (registry paths exist) and shows live QuantDesk numbers with dates and historical/hypothetical labels, degrading gracefully when the API is down.
The interactive widgets (noise-signal Bonferroni simulator, clustered-vs-naive simulator, survivorship simulator, PSR/DSR calculator) are deterministic for a seed and mirror backend formulas.
The Lab has a study selector (main / oos / insider_purchases) with clustered columns, the OOS confirmatory verdict block, and an in-sample vs OOS comparison. Missing studies show 'not run yet'.
The track-record page shows the chain head and verification status, with verify-it-yourself instructions.
There is no advice or buy/sell language anywhere, and every number is labelled historical or hypothetical with a date.
`npx tsc --noEmit` passes. Only owned paths are edited; globals.css only gets an appended '/* --- Learn --- */' section.
